Recently, Natalie Clark and her boyfriend, Billy LeBlanc,[ contracted Vibrio Vulnificus from eating raw oysters.](https://substack.com/redirect/7c97056e-3beb-486f-9325-e96a9cff28e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) LeBlanc, a Louisiana native, spent more than a week in the intensive care unit and Clark died.
Every year at about this time, I do my best to educate those who follow me about the[ dangers](https://substack.com/redirect/ab418836-f626-4680-9220-b8f31037951b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of Vibrio Vulnificus exposure, either by consuming raw seafood or via wound infection.
_**Short on time? Here 's the key points:**_
* Don't eat oysters raw, especially not in summer months/early fall;
* Avoid swimming in warm, brackish waters with cuts or open wounds, and;
* Expect vibrio to continue to migrate northward with climate change.

Mesoscale.News with Rebekah Jones is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..1bGig51GP1H5ysvBDt4O5WgbrLRYf9RaESoECipuwPA?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=146769130)
Globally, the various subtypes of [Vibrio bacteria ](https://substack.com/redirect/5544f0f9-ddb2-4ee7-a97e-e9da929cbb54?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)claim hundreds of thousands of lives each year. [Cholera ](https://substack.com/redirect/89e80517-36d8-4ef6-901a-3a030b7c0cec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)is one type of Vibrio and causes the most deaths annually of all Vibrio.
Vibrio infects about 80,000 people each year in the United States, with two-thirds of cases coming from consuming raw seafood.
_V. parahaemolyticus and[V. alginolyticus](https://substack.com/redirect/db5a958a-d9ec-4d04-9310-8c52ed94ab26?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) cause 40% and 20% of all Vibrio cases, and the fatality rate for each is 4% and 8%, respectively._
For Americans, the greatest risk is [Vibrio Vulnificus](https://substack.com/redirect/d293aebd-cdfd-461d-8244-87fd34a1184d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.**
V. Vulnificus (V.v.) may be far less common (only 10% of cases) but is [among the deadliest](https://substack.com/redirect/77979a4a-21fd-4ec2-a981-744ad8e1bca1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) \- 1 in 5 people infected die, usually within a few days. Vulnificus makes up 50% of all deaths from food-borne disease each year.
Vulnificus from wound infection (acquired from swimming in warm, brackish waters with cuts, scrapes or open wounds) can cause [necrotizing fasciitis](https://substack.com/redirect/b5eeae8e-a056-4c1c-a789-d9e139b75e8b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which causes your flesh to die. For this reason, V.v. is often referred to as a "flesh-eating" bacteria.
Wounds don't have to be large, either - small scrapes and cuts can become infected and kill a person within hours of infection.
And V.v. isn't the only danger in warm, brackish waters. You can also get [Naegleria fowleri ](https://substack.com/redirect/f3f69ad1-8553-4540-bf28-94f86b04542d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)swimming in those environments - that one is an amoeba that eats your brain and is fatal in 98% of cases.
* * *
_**Vibrio and climate change**_
Vibrio bacteria thrive in warm, brackish waters. The near-coastal waters of south Louisiana, for example, are prime breeding grounds for Vibrio bacteria.
Vibrio cases have been dramatically increasing in the last several decades.
Climate change amplifies the ability of vibrio to flourish in these environments. Vibrio incidences from consuming raw seafood [increased by more than 40%](https://substack.com/redirect/38a60b6d-c61b-4b19-b10f-b66a91980cc4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from 1996 to 2005. Including wound exposure, [total cases increased by 80%](https://substack.com/redirect/38a60b6d-c61b-4b19-b10f-b66a91980cc4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from 1996 to 2001 alone.
In a study over 30 years (1988-2018),1 V.v.[ cases caused by wound infections increased eightfold](https://substack.com/redirect/53f00666-81b4-4e88-88cc-9dc25096c0fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
About [75% of annual oyster harvests](https://substack.com/redirect/352140d1-b7a8-48a1-aec4-69635b716233?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) come from the Gulf Coast, and among those states Louisiana is the largest producer. Louisiana [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/72e9ae7d-fa2d-47e4-baf4-64bba01b7962?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Vulnificus cases nearly doubled over the 1988-1997 period in the following two decades.
"The salinity characteristics of estuaries are expected to change in the future due to more extreme weather events as well as sea level rise which will cause spatial and temporal changes to the salinity gradient and other physicochemical characteristics in coastal rivers," ([Baker-Austin et al. 2017](https://substack.com/redirect/2601fa71-dc3b-4a0e-84be-727010de7997?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg); [Dhillon and Inamdar 2014](https://substack.com/redirect/9827bb4a-5a16-43bb-be0a-756f4851ea32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)).
The northern-most limits of Vibrio have also shifted considerably since the 1980s. Last year saw the[ greatest spikes](https://substack.com/redirect/8811b9ec-8106-473b-a230-4f2986a76c20?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in cases not only in Louisiana, but in states as far north as New York, coinciding with the hottest year on record.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/23c85482-f98d-4432-ad35-ea31c5958931?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* * *
_**My own V.V. scare in Louisiana**_
July 2015 was the driest on record at the Rockefeller Wildlife Refuge in Vermillion Parish, Louisiana, where I spent two days teaching environmental science to an overnight camp for high school kids as part of my job with NOAA's Sea Grant program.
In the station's 62-year history, average precipitation for July was 7.25" in the Refuge. In July 2015, the area only registered 0.78". That July was also the hottest in more than a decade, with the highest nightly low temperature for the month in the station's history.
With increased evaporation and a lack of rainwater, the salinity of smaller water bodies typically too far inland and too fresh for breeding Vibrio increased. The conditions were ripe for a Vibrio bloom.
We went crabbing one afternoon for dinner and when casting my net, the rotten wood of the old dock I was standing on gave out and I fell into the water. My leg was shredded on the way down by the shell built up on the post.
I knew what was in the water. Between alligators, alligator gar and vibrio, I was out of the lake as soon as I went down. A colleague reached down to grab my hand to help me and said he had never seen someone "bounce" off the water that way.
My colleague ran to his truck, got a couple bottles of iodine from his first aid kit and just started pouring it all over my cut up leg. We rushed back to the dorm to check for antibiotics and to get bandages.
We had penicillin on hand, but since I was allergic, we had to go to the nearest medical clinic to find an alternative. The nearest facility was in Lake Charles, more than an hour away.
It took us 20 minutes to get back to the dorms, and another hour to get to the clinic. I wasn't seen for another 30 minutes after that, and wasn't able to get a prescription filled until almost two hours after that.
I spent four hours waiting to see if fever, swelling or anything out of the ordinary was setting in, knowing vulnificus can set in as little as two.
The panicked look on my coworkers face the entire drive back didn't help ease my anxiety.
Let's just say I'm very careful around piers and docks now.
And I hope this reminder will make you more cautious about eating raw shellfish and swimming in environments where vibrio thrives.

Every year at about this time, I do my best to educate those who follow me about the of Vibrio Vulnificus exposure, either by consuming raw seafood or via wound infection. Short on time? Here 's the key points: Don't eat oysters raw, especially not in summer months/early fall; Avoid swimming in warm, brackish waters with cuts or open wounds, and; Expect vibrio to continue to migrate northward with climate change. Mesoscale.News with Rebekah Jones is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. Globally, the various subtypes of hundreds of thousands of lives each year. one type of Vibrio and causes the most deaths annually of all Vibrio. Vibrio infects about 80,000 people each year in the United States, with two-thirds of cases coming from consuming raw seafood. V. parahaemolyticus and cause 40% and 20% of all Vibrio cases, and the fatality rate for each is 4% and 8%, respectively. For Americans, the greatest risk is . V. Vulnificus (V.v.) may be far less common (only 10% of cases) but is \- 1 in 5 people infected die, usually within a few days. Vulnificus makes up 50% of all deaths from food-borne disease each year. Vulnificus from wound infection (acquired from swimming in warm, brackish waters with cuts, scrapes or open wounds) can cause , which causes your flesh to die. For this reason, V.v. is often referred to as a "flesh-eating" bacteria. Wounds don't have to be large, either - small scrapes and cuts can become infected and kill a person within hours of infection. And V.v. isn't the only danger in warm, brackish waters. You can also get in those environments - that one is an amoeba that eats your brain and is fatal in 98% of cases. Vibrio and climate change Vibrio bacteria thrive in warm, brackish waters. The near-coastal waters of south Louisiana, for example, are prime breeding grounds for Vibrio bacteria. Vibrio cases have been dramatically increasing in the last several decades. Climate change amplifies the ability of vibrio to flourish in these environments. Vibrio incidences from consuming raw seafood from 1996 to 2005. Including wound exposure, from 1996 to 2001 alone. In a study over 30 years (1988-2018),1 V.v.. About come from the Gulf Coast, and among those states Louisiana is the largest producer. Louisiana that Vulnificus cases nearly doubled over the 1988-1997 period in the following two decades. "The salinity characteristics of estuaries are expected to change in the future due to more extreme weather events as well as sea level rise which will cause spatial and temporal changes to the salinity gradient and other physicochemical characteristics in coastal rivers," (; ). The northern-most limits of Vibrio have also shifted considerably since the 1980s. Last year saw the in cases not only in Louisiana, but in states as far north as New York, coinciding with the hottest year on record. | | ---|---|--- My own V.V. scare in Louisiana July 2015 was the driest on record at the Rockefeller Wildlife Refuge in Vermillion Parish, Louisiana, where I spent two days teaching environmental science to an overnight camp for high school kids as part of my job with NOAA's Sea Grant program. In the station's 62-year history, average precipitation for July was 7.25" in the Refuge. In July 2015, the area only registered 0.78". That July was also the hottest in more than a decade, with the highest nightly low temperature for the month in the station's history. With increased evaporation and a lack of rainwater, the salinity of smaller water bodies typically too far inland and too fresh for breeding Vibrio increased. The conditions were ripe for a Vibrio bloom. We went crabbing one afternoon for dinner and when casting my net, the rotten wood of the old dock I was standing on gave out and I fell into the water. My leg was shredded on the way down by the shell built up on the post. I knew what was in the water. Between alligators, alligator gar and vibrio, I was out of the lake as soon as I went down. A colleague reached down to grab my hand to help me and said he had never seen someone "bounce" off the water that way. My colleague ran to his truck, got a couple bottles of iodine from his first aid kit and just started pouring it all over my cut up leg. We rushed back to the dorm to check for antibiotics and to get bandages. We had penicillin on hand, but since I was allergic, we had to go to the nearest medical clinic to find an alternative. The nearest facility was in Lake Charles, more than an hour away. It took us 20 minutes to get back to the dorms, and another hour to get to the clinic. I wasn't seen for another 30 minutes after that, and wasn't able to get a prescription filled until almost two hours after that. I spent four hours waiting to see if fever, swelling or anything out of the ordinary was setting in, knowing vulnificus can set in as little as two. The panicked look on my coworkers face the entire drive back didn't help ease my anxiety. Let's just say I'm very careful around piers and docks now. And I hope this reminder will make you more cautious about eating raw shellfish and swimming in environments where vibrio thrives. # TESTIMONY
UPDATE SINCE OUR THERAPY:
Friends and Family,
Many of you have heard about Nena’s remarkable health transformation since she underwent Stem Cell Therapy. Her journey has been nothing short of miraculous. Her cancer, once at a daunting stage 5, has moved to stage 1. The wrinkles around her eyes have vanished, her hair has regrown in its original color, her eyesight has been restored to a perfect 20/20, and her energy levels have soared. She has even seen her insulin intake drop from 175 units a day to under 25. Her story is an incredible testament to the power of this therapy and she is still being healed daily. But today, I want to share my own testimony. Six weeks ago, I underwent this therapy, and the results have been nothing short of amazing. For years, I’ve suffered from chronic pain due to being bone-on-bone in my knees. This pain often led me to rely on narcotic pain medications and even walk with a cane. I was even granted permanent disability because of it. But just four days after the therapy, my knee pain completely disappeared. I have spent hours on my knees over the past five weeks, and the pain has not returned. My memory has cleared, my skin has cleared up, and my energy levels have skyrocketed. We are beyond excited about what God has done through this therapy, and we want to share this incredible opportunity with you. This is not a pyramid scheme or an MLM. It is a Christian-owned and operated company based in Texas, and Nena and I have spent hours fellowshipping with the owners. We believe in this therapy with all our hearts, and we want you to experience its transformative power. Don’t miss this opportunity. We will be holding a seminar with a free dinner for you to learn about this amazing, God-given therapy. Join us on Tuesday, the 23rd, in Torrance, California, and Wednesday, the 24th, in Modesto, California. Email me at officialderrickgates@gmail.com to register. This is your moment. Don’t let it pass you by.
Let's embrace this journey of transformation together!
Tag those that you think would benefit from this.
With gratitude and excitement,
Derrick & Nena To attend our Los Angeles Free Dinner on July 23rd in Torrance at 7pm or Modesto on July 24th at 7pm, please email me at officialderrickgates@gmail.com Previous Message: Can I share a profound testimony that has rocked our world and brought immense joy to my heart? My beloved wife, Nena, has been wrestling with relentless health challenges, including a fierce battle with cancer. In October 2020, we received the devastating news that she had six months to live. We pursued every method outside of chemotherapy. We had some success with alternative treatments, but it was at a cost of $6,000 a month, and we just could not afford it anymore. But today, seven weeks ago, a monumental shift occurred in our lives. Nena underwent stem cell therapy, and the transformation has been nothing short of miraculous. Let me paint a picture of this incredible journey: Firstly, her insulin levels plummeted by a staggering 75%. Now, Nena has been reliant on insulin since childhood, making this a profound and life-changing development. Secondly, her vision, once clouded and aided by bifocals, has been restored to a sharp 20/20. Wrinkles have vanished, and her hair has reclaimed its natural color. Her hemoglobin levels, previously alarmingly low, have shown marked improvement. And most significantly, her cancer has regressed to stage 1 from stage 4. This, my friends, is undeniably a God-sized miracle. We are bursting with gratitude and a deep desire to share this miracle with all of you, our cherished friends and family. On the 23rd of this month, my dear friend Pastor James Fortune will share his wisdom in another enlightening seminar on stem cell therapy. Stem cell therapy isn't just a hope or a promise; it's a reality that has yielded remarkable results across various ailments. From cancer to thyroid issues, weight management to hair regrowth, chemical imbalances to hormone problems, and even autism, stem cell therapy has shown incredible promise of hope. And I assure you, this isn't about a high-pressure sales pitch. We want you to join us, to learn, to share in our joy, and to enjoy a complimentary dinner as a token of our appreciation. If this resonates with you and you seek hope and healing, please fill out the form using the link provided. I promise you an evening of enlightenment, community, and, above all, hope. Together, let's embrace the possibilities of a brighter, healthier tomorrow. Thank you. PS. If you are not in driving distance to LA and you are interested we can come and do a seminar for you in your area. We will even pick up the tab. You will not regret this. If this is of interest to you please email me at officialderrickgates@gmail.com Love you all Derrick Gates You can also watch Nena talk about her Testimony with Pastor James Fortune Below,

Hi, Patriot.

I haven't introduced myself to you in a while, and I want you to understand why I believe what I do.

I was born and raised in Houston, TX in a military family. I was honored to accept an appointment to the United States Military Academy at West Point to begin my career.

[](https://click.historyoftheday.com/u/click?_t=930f96a60371422687dbefcfca24c32b&_m=9e9af92c0c104b18a60310bd46cd73b3&_e=8JJJrtW0WkCI65xwG7z5gD6-CG9VrfKhJTb1kcKbE2NyVIbxlsspUBJfNCei8seTBf8WA0xFzpJEZWmK6JLCPEnrXbcBKT6UjzoXp_YOj3hjUfpwIySWoMX485bqAoppDgslJL8I4KC39mEC__PQ963eTovHWBSKistB0ebYf1xBMT-7urPHcoatgp8S3JdHUimGoi9puXgZ4-LqWf2sJuNo6wSstoK9po3RsUGwrcYh7KA1MC52EQy-KCu2ZN2WoT8yaTvFFZ7ikn_rQwgZrf3C_2Ex0BmF0DAqLbmaQdFtZKKI_5w_uCIWY24drHFKX7GGpQKD49CyOTHHwQAhtWS3BimZC4K8-3X-gAoOTwwSFEncVNxdCrbTptA6v_qU)
In 2004, I received my commission in the U.S. Army and graduated with a Bachelor of Science degree in Leadership and Management with a Field of Study in Mechanical Engineering. After West Point, I spent eight years in the Army as an Aviation Branch Officer and AH-64D Apache Longbow helicopter pilot.

[](https://click.historyoftheday.com/u/click?_t=930f96a60371422687dbefcfca24c32b&_m=9e9af92c0c104b18a60310bd46cd73b3&_e=8JJJrtW0WkCI65xwG7z5gD6-CG9VrfKhJTb1kcKbE2NyVIbxlsspUBJfNCei8seTBf8WA0xFzpJEZWmK6JLCPEnrXbcBKT6UjzoXp_YOj3hjUfpwIySWoMX485bqAoppDgslJL8I4KC39mEC__PQ963eTovHWBSKistB0ebYf1xBMT-7urPHcoatgp8S3JdHUimGoi9puXgZ4-LqWf2sJuNo6wSstoK9po3RsUGwrcYiuJuXy3vYJJrI_e6rhNeAG29xfFCDu71JnyV0AskWVJzPJOqdDsSyLhG9YOlY-YAB-PDnfJoBrLJCR97zWldt1Mxjf5N42bEfQhPUCzs4UYOCXZNZ0hCyWBMgDY6ISvJqLn2Dq-qrXHjAhI5rxH3k)
I'm proud to share that my service included one combat deployment to Iraq, and two deployments to Saudi Arabia where I served as a Diplomatic Liaison Officer.

After honorably discharging as a Captain, I attended Cornell University and earned a Master of Business Administration (M.B.A.), a Master of Public Administration (M.P.A.) and a Master of Industrial and Labor Relations (M.I.L.R.).

I never believed that changing Washington would be easy, but graduating from West Point and serving in the United States Army, being deployed to combat zones, and flying Apache helicopters over Iraq has prepared me for tough fights and big challenges. I truly believe nothing is more worth fighting for than our great country and our way of life in the Houston area.

My family is everything to me. My wife Emily and I have two daughters and one son, Victoria, Olivia and Willie Parish Hunt 2nd.

[](https://click.historyoftheday.com/u/click?_t=930f96a60371422687dbefcfca24c32b&_m=9e9af92c0c104b18a60310bd46cd73b3&_e=8JJJrtW0WkCI65xwG7z5gD6-CG9VrfKhJTb1kcKbE2NyVIbxlsspUBJfNCei8seTBf8WA0xFzpJEZWmK6JLCPEnrXbcBKT6UjzoXp_YOj3hjUfpwIySWoMX485bqAoppDgslJL8I4KC39mEC__PQ963eTovHWBSKistB0ebYf1xBMT-7urPHcoatgp8S3JdHUimGoi9puXgZ4-LqWf2sJuNo6wSstoK9po3RsUGwrcbtP8U5cTEqhbRruZ41eer0xQkZS4mfy-fkLd2gPhckOo8rCMyXpODy9j-RZrm0oVG0Rd6W4uS8inPd78i_m8FWdrY3zAMHV_amE021-x3f28XdyoKtIgJxkHpGGykyiAkGhK1KsiYOCY-8M0kH5OQj)
As the great-great grandson of a slave, serving as a Congressman in the U.S. The House of Representatives is truly in the wildest dreams of my ancestors. It's the honor of a lifetime to serve this great country and the Great State of Texas, but I can't keep doing it without your support.

body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tk-2024-suhas [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tk-2024-suhas]
The road to a Democratic majority in the House runs straight through Virginia. I’m proud to support strong VA Democrats who are running for U.S. House seats, and I hope you’ll join me by reading these emails and chipping in when you can. With your help, we can flip the House and keep VA blue! —Tim
Hi friends, it’s Suhas Subramanyam, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Congress in Virginia’s 10th Congressional District.
I’m running to tackle some of our biggest issues in the House — like building up a strong economy for all, defending abortion rights from MAGA extremists, reducing gun violence in our communities, and continuing to deliver progress for Virginians, like I’ve been doing since I was elected to the Virginia General Assembly in 2019.
I’m proud to have the endorsement of Senator Tim Kaine, and as one of his longtime supporters, I’m asking for your help today: Will you split a donation of any amount between Senator Kaine’s re-election campaign and my campaign for Congress? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tk-2024-suhas]
I was inspired to serve others back in college when I volunteered to help rebuild the communities affected by Hurricane Katrina. Since then, I’ve been proud to serve in the White House as a technology policy advisor to President Obama, as a volunteer EMT and firefighter in Loudoun County, and these days, as a Virginia State Senator.
While serving in the General Assembly, I’ve worked to lower prescription drug costs, crack down on toll spikes for commuters, and secure millions of dollars in refunds on energy bills for VA families.
And as a husband and father of two, there’s nothing more important to me than ensuring safe communities for our families and a better future for our children.
I’m running for Congress to stand strong against MAGA extremists, defend essential freedoms like abortion rights, and work across the aisle when needed to deliver real progress for Virginians and Americans.
I’m also incredibly proud to say I’ve been endorsed by incumbent Representative Jennifer Wexton, who flipped the 10th District from red to blue back in 2018!
This November, we have a chance to keep this district blue (and help flip the House!) — but I’m going to need your help. Will you split a donation between me and Tim Kaine to power our campaigns through November? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tk-2024-suhas]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tk-2024-suhas]
Thanks so much for reading, and for supporting candidates like me who are working to keep Virginia blue this November.
Sincerely,
Suhas

Suhas Subramanyam

subject: Kari Lake’s remarks, and our path forward
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
We always knew that this would be one of the closest races in the country. That’s no secret. But we’ve been really fortunate so far because month after month we have absolutely crushed Kari Lake’s fundraising numbers. That gives us a tremendous advantage, and it lets us deliver our message to the people who need to hear it.
#

Peter, Kari Lake directly addressed the Republican National Convention this week.
She had a prime-time slot, one of the biggest of the night. I’m not going to speculate on how many people watched, but I can tell you one thing for sure: It was the biggest platform she’s ever had.
We always knew that this would be one of the closest races in the country. That’s no secret. But we’ve been really fortunate so far because month after month we have absolutely crushed Kari Lake’s fundraising numbers. That gives us a tremendous advantage, and it lets us deliver our message to the people who need to hear it.
All that could change in an instant, though. The kind of national attention that Kari Lake got at the RNC could turn into millions of dollars raised in the blink of an eye. Big donors send in massive checks, the millions of MAGA faithful add their donations, and before you know it we’re the ones getting crushed. It’s Kari Lake’s ads flooding the airwaves and our chances at defending Arizona and holding the U.S. Senate collapse.
The only way we’ll prevent that from happening is if we continue to raise the resources we need to win.
I need you with me. It’s as simple as that.

During a period of homelessness, James registered to vote using the address of the barbershop where he worked. The letter made it clear: his voter registration could be canceled if he didn't take action. His challenger? One of a handful of right-wing self-appointed activists who are attempting to purge Georgia’s voter rolls ahead of the presidential election. body:
But we can’t wallow

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/89126316/486276274/-1463099547?refcode=-header-&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS8xMDMxMTgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNWMzMDZhN2ItNTk0NS1lZjExLTg2YzMtNjA0NWJkZDllMDk2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=mjghm5GELl5vWYWaN2kl2VxyZVaZ-ZlB9O9wwrcH8gE=) | Peter, Like many of you, I am feeling pretty depressed right now about the state of our politics. Republicans are rallying behind Donald Trump and JD Vance at their GOP convention this week and we all see the news around President Biden. I sent you an email earlier this week sharing my fears about what this national environment means for toss-up races like mine. But I refuse to let this stop our mission. We simply have too much at stake to hide our heads in the sand. Abortion access, climate, our democracy - all are on the line. **So this week I told my team we have to act. We have to fight back. We have to get our message out to voters and tell them what Democrats stand for.** I know everyone is freaking out, but there is no more time to waste. We need everyone to get off the sidelines and fight for our values. We must remind ourselves of the true character of Donald Trump:
